plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub native to Mexico with small yellow flowers (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In frost-free regions it grows into a large landscape shrub, and elsewhere it is a popular potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown worldwide in tropical and subtropical gardens and as an indoor plant
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants that need about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for roughly 5 weeks to develop their colorful bracts.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions and blooms when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense clusters of large, vivid flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere's early summer it is one of the most spectacular flowering trees in tropical and subtropical regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); varies in the tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in northern Australia, Brazil, southern Africa, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: It is considered endangered in its native Madagascar even though it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and delicate, slightly fragrant flowers that open in the cooler months. It is more sun-tolerant than its relative Camellia japonica and is often used for hedges and espaliers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to mid-winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Japan, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce a culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Christmas Bush (Ceratopetalum gummiferum)
plants.description: An Australian native shrub or small tree whose small white flowers fade as the sepals enlarge and turn a brilliant red. It is a seasonal favorite in cut flower arrangements during the southern summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to December)
plants.location: Native to the eastern coast of New South Wales, Australia, in sandstone gullies and woodlands
plants.funFact: The red color comes not from petals but from enlarged calyx lobes, and it is used in Australia as a Christmas decoration much as holly is in the Northern Hemisphere.
